messages.tip.action_button: Runs this action using the current data and parameter values.
messages.tip.angle: Minimum angular separation, in degrees, between accepted density maxima. Larger values keep fewer, more widely separated hoved poles; smaller values may retain nearby peaks from the same orientation familie.
messages.tip.bins: Sets the KDE density-grid level as 2^N cells per axis. Higher values reveal finer density detail but require more memory and computation. Use the lowest value that resolves stable density maxima.
messages.tip.classify_action: Assigns each point to the closest reviewed hoved pole within the JS cone threshold and writes the JS skalarfelt. The reviewed pole table, not the original automatic peaks, is used.
messages.tip.colour.dof: Select the number of rotation degrees of freedom. Use 2 for the original two-angle rotation model or 3 for the intrinsic Z-Y-X Euler rotation used by the three-degree-of-freedom model.
messages.tip.colour.objective: Select the objective function minimised during optimisation. It controls how the rotated pole orientations are penalised or distributed in the colour reference system.
messages.tip.colour.subsample: Percentage of valid point normaler used during optimisation. Lower percentages reduce computation time; 100% uses all valid normaler.
messages.tip.colour.iterations: Maksimum number of differential-evolution generations. Higher values allow a more extensive search but increase computation time.
messages.tip.colour.population: Population multiplier used by differential evolution. Larger values evaluate more candidate rotations per generation, increasing search effort and computation time.
messages.tip.colour.seed: Optional integer random seed. Enter a value to make the sampling and optimisation reproducible; leave blank to use a new random seed.
messages.tip.colour.export_copy: Creates a new CloudCompare punktsky coloured using the selected colour space and the selected pole space. The original punktsky is not modified.
messages.tip.colour.show_density: Displays the relative pole-density distribution obtained with the optimised rotation. It does not run the optimisation again.
messages.tip.colour.show_poles: Displays the point-normal poles after applying the optimised rotation, using the selected stereonet projection.
messages.tip.clouds: When fasetter are created, also creates one separate punktsky for each endelig klynge. Disable this for very large datasets if the additional clouds use too much memory.
messages.tip.cluster: Runs DBSCAN independently within each positive JS familie, estimates a familie-specific eps, removes components smaller than ppcluster, fits plan equations, and writes cl, A, B, C, D and sigma using the original global point indices.
messages.tip.colour.optimise: Starts the normal-colour optimisation with the parameters entered above and determines the rotation angles that minimise the selected objective function.
messages.tip.dbscanminpts: Minimum number of points inside the DBSCAN neighbourhood, including the point itself, required for a core point. The MATLAB method uses 4. Increasing this value requires denser neighbourhoods and may classify more points as noise.
messages.tip.density_action: Calculates the KDE pole-density surface and extracts automatic hoved poles. Review and, if necessary, edit the resulting pole table before assigning JS familier.
messages.tip.editable_param: Editable parameter. Enter a numeric value where appropriate; the associated label indicates the units and the parameter effect.
messages.tip.facets: Creates one convex planar mesh for each valid endelig klynge using its stored global point indices and fitted plan. Clustering must be completed first.
messages.tip.family_clouds: After clustering, creates one punktsky for each positive JS familie. Each punktsky contains that familie’s points and retains the JS, cl and plan skalarfelt.
messages.tip.family_plot_action: Plots point normaler coloured by their current JS value and overlays the reviewed hoved poles. This is available only when JS corresponds to the current reviewed pole table.
messages.tip.fix: When selected, each klynge in a JS familie uses the reviewed familie-pole normal and derives only D from the klynge centroid. When cleared, each klynge normal is fitted locally using PCA/SVD.
messages.tip.jscone: Maksimum angular difference, in degrees, between a point normal and a reviewed hoved pole. The closest pole inside this cone defines JS; points outside all cones receive JS=0.
messages.tip.kneighbor: Neighbour order used to estimate eps separately for each JS familie. The MATLAB method uses K=4 and queries K+1 neighbours because the first result is the point itself. Larger K represents a broader local spacing scale.
messages.tip.ksigma: Multiplier in eps = mean(unique KNN distances) + k_sigma × sample standard deviation. The MATLAB method uses 2. Larger values increase eps and tend to join components across wider gaps; smaller values tend to split klynger.
messages.tip.labels: Shows cardinal directions, angular guides and stereonet annotations. These guides are visual only and do not affect the calculations.
messages.tip.maxpoles: Maksimum number of automatic hoved poles retained from the density surface. It limits the candidate JS familier; the reviewed pole table remains authoritative and can be edited manually.
messages.tip.merge: Coplanarity threshold based on |Di-Dj|/(sigma_i+sigma_j). Larger values merge more same-familie klynger into a common plan; smaller values preserve more separate plan. Set 0 to disable this merge.
messages.tip.minclustersize: Minimum component size after DBSCAN, corresponding to MATLAB ppcluster. Components with fewer points are rejected and assigned cl=0. This does not control whether a point is a DBSCAN core point.
messages.tip.plot_poles: Plots all valid point normaler as poles on the selected stereonet projection. This is a visual inspection step and does not modify the punktsky.
messages.tip.pole_add: Adds a new hoved pole from the Fallretning and Fall values. The table and density plot update immediately; familie IDs are renumbered and existing JS and klynge results become outdated.
messages.tip.pole_apply: Applies the Fallretning and Fall values to the selected hoved pole. The reviewed table becomes the source of truth, so JS classification and clustering must then be recalculated.
messages.tip.pole_delete: Deletes the selected hoved pole, renumbers the remaining familier and refreshes the plot. Existing JS and klynge results become outdated.
messages.tip.pole_down: Moves the selected pole one row down. Because table order defines J_1, J_2, etc., this changes familie IDs and requires JS classification and clustering to be recalculated.
messages.tip.pole_move: Changes the familie order. Because familie IDs follow table order, changing the order requires JS classification and clustering to be recalculated.
messages.tip.pole_table: Authoritative reviewed list of hoved poles. JS classification, familie plots, Fisher K and subsequent clustering use this exact order and orientation. Editing or reordering the table invalidates existing JS and klynge results.
messages.tip.pole_up: Moves the selected pole one row up. Because table order defines J_1, J_2, etc., this changes familie IDs and requires JS classification and clustering to be recalculated.
messages.tip.poles.source: Choose whether pole plots, density and automatic peak detection use the original normaler or normaler transformed by the optimised rotation. Stored hoved-pole orientations always remain in the original reference system.
messages.tip.projection: Selects the stereographic projection used for plots. Likvinklet preserves angular relationships; equal-area preserves area. This setting changes only the visual projection, not the original point normaler or skalarfelt.
messages.tip.refresh: Refreshes the selected CloudCompare entity and checks which workflow actions and Verktøy commands have the data required to run.
messages.tip.seed: Optional integer used only with Tilfeldig klynge ordering. The same seed reproduces the numbering; leave blank to generate a new random order for each run.
messages.tip.show_density: Displays the last computed density and current hoved poles without recalculating the KDE or detecting peaks.
messages.tip.sort: Controls endelig cl numbering within each JS familie. Size orders the largest klynger first, D follows their spatial position along the fitted normal, and Tilfeldig shuffles the order. IDs restart at 1 for each familie.
messages.tip.style: Chooses line contours or filled contours for the density plot. This changes visualisation only; density values and detected poles are not recalculated.

messages.about.body:
Authors:
  Adrián Riquelme Guill
  Roberto Tomás Jover
  Antonio Abellán Fernández
  University of Alicante

Scientific references:
  Riquelme, A.J., Abellan, A., Tomas, R., & Jaboyedoff, M. (2014).
  A new approach for semi-automatic rock mass joints recognition
  from 3D point clouds. Computers & Geosciences, 68, 38-52.
  https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cageo.2014.03.014

  Riquelme, A.J., Abellan, A., & Tomas, R. (2015).
  Discontinuity spacing analysis in rock masses using 3D point clouds.
  Engineering Geology, 195, 185-195.
  https://doi.org/10.1016/j.enggeo.2015.06.009

  Riquelme, A., Tomas, R., Cano, M., Pastor, J.L., & Abellan, A. (2018).
  Automatic mapping of discontinuity persistence on rock masses using
  3D point clouds. Rock Mechanics and Rock Engineering, 51, 3005-3028.
  https://doi.org/10.1007/s00603-018-1519-9

  Riquelme, A., Tomas, R., Cano, M., Pastor, J.L., & Abellan, A. (2026).
  Orientation-based colour mapping and spherical density analysis for
  rock discontinuity detection in 3D point clouds of roadcut slopes.
  Journal of Rock Mechanics and Geotechnical Engineering.
  https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jrmge.2025.12.059

  Riquelme Guill, A. (2015).
  Uso de nubes de puntos 3D para identificación y caracterización de
  familias de discontinuidades planas en afloramientos rocosos y
  evaluación de la calidad geomecánica. Doctoral thesis, University of
  Alicante.
  https://rua.ua.es/entities/publication/78d254b9-1a7b-49b1-a35a-c0edbdeeb225

Based on:
  Adrian Riquelme's MATLAB implementation of the Discontinuity Set
  Extractor (DSE), Department of Civil Engineering, University of
  Alicante, Spain.

Libraries and algorithms:
  - NumPy: numerical arrays and vector operations.
  - SciPy: KDE, differential evolution, nearest-neighbour queries,
    connected components and convex-hull geometry.
  - Matplotlib: stereonet, density and analysis plotting.
  - colorcet: scientific and perceptually useful colour maps used by
    the klynge visualisation.
  - Pillow: icon loading, resizing and GUI icon normalisation.
  - CloudCompare / pycc: point-punktsky, normal and scalar-field access.
  - Tkinter / ttk: graphical user interface.
  - PyVista (optional): interactive 3D normal/sphere visualisation.

  Algorithms and methods:
  - DSE hoved-pole extraction using spherical/steronet KDE, based on
    the Botev et al. kernel-density approach.
  - Differential Evolution for normal-colour rotation optimisation.
  - DBSCAN (Ester et al., 1996) for spatial clustering of discontinuity
    familier.
  - Fisher directional statistics for mean-pole concentration and
    confidence intervals.
  - cKDTree nearest-neighbour searches and Qhull convex-hull geometry
    through SciPy.

Acknowledgments:
  CloudCompare development team and the researchers whose methods
  underpin the DSE workflow.
